questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a facilitative message?
questions.explanation: Questions used in clinical interviews can be either facilitative or obstructive. Facilitative messages help the interview to flow, establish rapport, and gain the confidence of the patient. For example, open-ended questions, facilitating statements, reflections, silence, interpretations, positive reinforcements, etc. Run on or polythematic questioning refers to the process of asking the patient a number of questions at the same time. For example, ‘Have you felt high in spirits, gone on spending sprees, and made foolish investments in the past week?’ These questions can be obstructive. Self-disclosures are statements about oneself (the psychiatrist) that may help establish rapport with the patient. 'I want' messages are generally used when the interview fails to progress because the patient is stuck on the same topic. In this case, the psychiatrist could say politely that he or she wants to move on to other topics

questions.question_text: A psychiatrist at an early stage of his initial assessment interview asks the patient, ‘Can you tell me about your depression?’ Which of the following interview techniques is he utilizing ?
questions.explanation: Open-ended questions reflect a topic that the psychiatrist may want to explore, but leave it open to the patient to say what he/she thinks is important. These questions are used to start the interview and, later on, can lead to specific closed-ended questions. Put down questions are where the underlying message is a criticism. For example, ‘How can you complain when you have got an A grade in your GCSE?’ Facilitation statements encourage the patient to continue along a particular line of thought. For example, statements such as ‘Go on’; ‘Proceed’; ‘What else’ are facilitation statements

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an open-ended question?

options.text: Could you tell me the name of the prime minister?
It seems as if you feel people are against you?
What do you find stressful in your job?
Do you have trouble falling asleep?

questions.explanation: A question whose answer cannot be a simple yes or no, or a single factual answer that can be classified as right or wrong, is an open-ended question, such as the question given in 3. A. (See also Question 2)

questions.question_text: During a clinical interview the following statement is made by the clinician: ‘So you have been anxious since these changes occurred at your workplace.’ Which of the following interview techniques best describes the above statement?
questions.explanation: Reflections are statements where the psychiatrist repeats what the patient has just said. This gives an opportunity to correct one’s understanding of what the patient said and to let the patient know that the clinician is listening and trying to understand the situation the patient is in

questions.question_text: Which of the following interview techniques is least directive?
questions.explanation: Directiveness in the interview ensures that a clinician has all the information needed from a patient. Highly directive intervention aims to focus and restrict the patient’s speech content and behavior. These may include checklists or yes/no questions. Limit setting and redirection include situations where a clinician attempts to change the direction of the interview, especially when the interview is not progressing in the detail of information transferred

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a supportive intervention during a clinical interview process?
questions.explanation: Being empathetic and acknowledging a patient’s emotional state helps in facilitating progression of clinical interview. These are supportive interventions required in various degrees by patients. Summarization is not an intervention but a technique facilitating a clinician’s understanding of a patient’s story. Confrontation may be helpful in some situations, but it cannot be considered as a supportive intervention during clinical interview

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is true when inquiring about suicidal ideation?

options.text: This should not be asked unless the patient volunteers information
Asking about suicidal ideation can instill suicidal ideas in a person
A person who intends to attempt suicide will never divulge
Passive suicidal ideas must be inquired further for any plans made
The aim of the assessment is to corner the patient into a disclosure

correct_answer.text: Passive suicidal ideas must be inquired further for any plans made

correct_answers.text: Passive suicidal ideas must be inquired further for any plans made

questions.explanation: Thoughts of self-harm should always be inquired about. Contemplation of suicide is very common among the mentally ill. There is no evidence that inquiring about suicidal ideations increases the risk of committing suicide. In fact, many patients would welcome an opportunity to discuss any suicidal thoughts with a professional

questions.question_text: ‘Do you ever hear voices commenting on what you are doing?’ This question is usually asked to ascertain the presence of which one of the following?
questions.explanation: First rank symptoms (FRS), proposed by Kurt Schneider, suggest a diagnosis of schizophrenia. These symptoms are not specific for schizophrenia. The prevalence of FRS in schizophrenia ranges from 28% to 72%. First rank symptoms do not carry any prognostic significance. The stated question in this case inquires for the presence of ‘running commentary’ hallucinations – voices commenting on patients’ thoughts or actions

questions.question_text: Regarding the Mini Mental State Examination (MMSE), which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The subject is asked to guess the answer if unsure
If a person scores 3 on serial sevens, and scores 4 on spelling WORLD backwards then the score for attention is 3
On the reading test one point is scored if the patient reads ‘Close your eyes’ out loud
Education affects the rate of change of scores in normal and dementia subjects
MMSE scores are not affected by the socioeconomic status of a subject

correct_answer.text: The subject is asked to guess the answer if unsure

correct_answers.text: The subject is asked to guess the answer if unsure

questions.explanation: While administering the MMSE, the subject is asked to guess the answer if he is unsure. This could possibly differentiate patients with pseudodementia who usually answer ‘I don’t know’ while truly demented patients often give wrong responses

questions.question_text: Assessment of insight is an integral part of mental state examination in psychiatric practice. Regarding insight, which of the following statements is true?

options.text: Patients with schizophrenia will never have insight into their illness
OCD, being a neurosis, insight is always intact
Intellectual insight is present when patients’ awareness and understanding of their symptoms lead to a change in behavior
Intellectual insight is the highest level of insight
Loss of insight is similar to the concept of anosognosia in neurological illness

correct_answer.text: Loss of insight is similar to the concept of anosognosia in neurological illness

correct_answers.text: Loss of insight is similar to the concept of anosognosia in neurological illness

questions.explanation: The three dimensions of insight proposed by David include: the ability to label unusual experiences as pathological, to recognize that one has mental illness, and to comply with treatment

questions.question_text: A patient with schizophrenia vividly describes how Martians are ‘reverse freezing’ earth to produce global warming. He stops to ask what you think about this. Choose the best response

options.text: This is a fantastic theory. But I want to know more about this. Tell me, have you ever seen these Martians?
This seems possible but there is no proof for all this. Tell me, have you ever seen these Martians?
This cannot be true. Martians do not exist. Tell me, have you ever seen these Martians?
Tell me, have you ever seen these Martians?
What I think is not so important. I want to know more about what you think of this. Tell me, have you ever seen these Martians?

correct_answer.text: What I think is not so important. I want to know more about what you think of this. Tell me, have you ever seen these Martians?

correct_answers.text: What I think is not so important. I want to know more about what you think of this. Tell me, have you ever seen these Martians?

questions.explanation: Option A and B indicate collusion with the patient’s belief. Option C is a direct confrontation while D is evasion from the topic which can reduce engagement

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is NOT an advisable first response when a patient discloses past sexual abuse at a clinical encounter?

options.text: Ask if she wants to say anything more about this now
Ask if she has ever disclosed this to anyone
Ask if she sees a link between this and her current difficulties

questions.explanation: Childhood physical, sexual abuse, and neglect are extremely common experiences among those who develop serious mental health problems

questions.question_text: Closed questions are best avoided in which of the following scenarios?

options.text: A guarded patient not answering spontaneously
A suggestible patient with learning difficulty
A psychotic patient who is actively hallucinating

correct_answer.text: A suggestible patient with learning difficulty

correct_answers.text: A suggestible patient with learning difficulty

questions.explanation: While interviewing people with limited intelligence, questions should be brief and worded in a simple way

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the single best question to discern premorbid personality of a patient?

options.text: How would your friends describe you?
What were you like before you became unwell?
If we had met 10 years ago, what sort of person would I be talking to?

questions.explanation: There is no single question that can reliably elicit premorbid personality traits

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a discriminating question to screen for harmful use of alcohol?

options.text: Have you ever attempted to cut down your drinking?
Do you get annoyed when people talk about your drinking?
Have you ever felt guilty for drinking excessively?
Do you need a drink as soon as you wake up?

questions.explanation: The CAGE questionnaire includes questions on ‘Cut down’, ‘Annoyed’, ‘Guilty’, and ‘Eye opener’

questions.question_text: A patient looks disheveled, with unkempt hair and dirty, unwashed clothes. Self-neglect is commonly noted in all of the following EXCEPT
questions.explanation: While self-neglect can be seen in any severe mental illness, it is not very common in isolated anxiety disorders

questions.question_text: A 57-year-old lady with many previous hospitalizations is brought by police to casualty. She is wearing full make-up, green lipstick, shiny green nail polish, and green jewelry. She asks everyone at the admission unit to call her Ms Green. Which of the following diagnoses is most consistent with the above presentation?
questions.explanation: Exuberant dressing and makeup suggests elevated mood

questions.question_text: Which of the following domains of cognition is tested by administering Serial Sevens Test?
questions.explanation: Serial sevens test is a part of Mini Mental State Examination

questions.question_text: A 33-year-old man attending an out-patient clinic turns towards his left and spits out, muttering unintelligibly. He does this act at least three times in half an hour and appears very guarded. This gesture is suggestive of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Hallucinatory behaviors, such as the one described in this example, are often noted in acutely psychotic patients with poor insight

questions.question_text: A depressed patient does not smile or laugh when a joke is shared by a fellow patient. She shows a defect in which of the following aspects of mental state examination?
questions.explanation: Reactivity of affect refers to change in affect in response to environmental cues

questions.question_text: An elderly patient in a stroke ward laughs all of a sudden inappropriately, and within a few minutes becomes tearful and cries for no reason. She exhibits an abnormality in which of the following aspects of mental state examination?
questions.explanation: Stability of affect refers to maintaining a particular affective state for a reasonable period of time

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the major difference between mood and affect in mental state examination?

options.text: Mood is short-lived while affect is longer lasting
Mood is objective while affect is subjective
Affect is transient but difficult to interpret

questions.explanation: Various schools of thought exist in distinguishing mood from affect

questions.question_text: Nihilistic delusions will be congruent with which of the following findings of mental state examination?
questions.explanation: Nihilism is similar to pessimism with self-reference of an extreme belief

questions.question_text: When eliciting suicide risk, which of the following questions should be avoided if possible?

options.text: Do you have any plans to kill yourself?
How are you feeling in your mood?
Have you ever considered life is not worth living?
Have you ever wanted to go to sleep and never wake up?

questions.explanation: Direct questioning about suicidality does not increase the risk of suicide

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a manifestation of hypothyroidism?

options.text: Sparing of the posterior column sensations

correct_answer.text: Sparing of the posterior column sensations

correct_answers.text: Sparing of the posterior column sensations

questions.explanation: Features suggestive of hypothyroidism include slowing of EEG, excessive daytime sleepiness, hypothermia, cerebellar ataxia, dementia, and psychosis

questions.question_text: Russell’s sign is usually associated with which one of the following disorders?
questions.explanation: Russell’s sign was first described in bulimia nervosa

questions.question_text: On physical examination, you notice that a person with a history of substance misuse now has piloerection, dilated pupils, rhinorrhea, and he is yawning frequently. Withdrawal from which of the following substances can cause this presentation?
questions.explanation: These features are suggestive of opiate withdrawal

questions.question_text: A 50-year-old patient was brought to the A and E department in a confused state. On physical examination he has nystagmus, ocular palsy, and ataxia. Which of the following parts of clinical assessment is likely to be most relevant to this presentation?
questions.explanation: The features of acute confusion, nystagmus, ocular palsy, and ataxia are suggestive of Wernicke’s encephalopathy, possibly secondary to alcohol use in a 50-year-old male

questions.question_text: An 18-year-old male, recently started on a medication, presents to the A&E department with slow, long-sustained, contorting, involuntary movements and postures involving proximal limb and axial muscles. Which of the following medications is most likely to cause the above presentation?
questions.explanation: The clinical situation given here is an example of an acute dystonic reaction in a young male, possibly a psychotic patient, who has been started on an antipsychotic

questions.question_text: A 21-year-old female presented to the emergency department with complaints of recurrent attacks of severe dizziness, lasting for 10 to 20 minutes. On examination during the episode of dizziness, there was no evidence of nystagmus. Which one of the following is true?

options.text: Her symptoms may be associated with fear of going to places from where escape is impossible
Vertigo without nystagmus is suggestive of central vertigo of brainstem origin
Antihistaminic medications are likely to be effective in this case

correct_answer.text: Her symptoms may be associated with fear of going to places from where escape is impossible

correct_answers.text: Her symptoms may be associated with fear of going to places from where escape is impossible

questions.explanation: Absence of nystagmus during an attack of dizziness almost always rules out vertigo secondary to labyrinthine or brain stem pathology

questions.question_text: A sudden onset of chorea is least likely in which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: The onset of Huntington’s disease is invariably insidious and gradually progressing

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of subacute combined degeneration of the spinal cord?
questions.explanation: Features suggestive of subacute combined degeneration of the cord (SACD) include paraesthesias, difficulties with gait and balance, and signs of posterior column dysfunction

questions.question_text: Which of the following physical symptoms is seen in factitious disorder?
questions.explanation: Factitious disorder is a condition where clinical symptoms are consciously and intentionally produced by the patient

questions.question_text: A man admitted to the psychiatric intensive care unit with a manic episode, received 10 mg of haloperidol intramuscularly as he had turned violent. He became unresponsive shortly afterwards. On examination, there is evidence of confusion, labile BP, hyperthermia, rigidity, and dysphagia. What is the most important differential diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome is a medical emergency that can occur when treating a patient with antipsychotics

questions.question_text: Which of the following questionnaires is used to identify psychiatric ‘caseness’ in the general population?
questions.explanation: General health questionnaire (GHQ) is used to define psychiatric ‘caseness’ in epidemiological studies

questions.question_text: Characteristic feature of Argyll Robertson pupil include all of the following EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Argyll Robertson pupil (ARP) is characteristically associated with neurosyphilis

questions.question_text: Thunderclap headache is highly suggestive of which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Thunderclap headaches are sudden onset, severe headaches radiating behind the occiput with some degree of associated neck stiffness

questions.question_text: Waddling gait is characteristic of which of the following neurological difficulties?
questions.explanation: Waddling gait is seen with severe proximal muscle weakness

questions.question_text: A 59-year-old man has a small, spastic tongue with significant difficulty in pronouncing consonants. On neurological examination, he has a brisk jaw jerk. Which of the following is the most likely explanation for the above presentation?
questions.explanation: Bilateral upper motor neurone lesions of the corticobulbar tract result in pseudobulbar or spastic dysarthria

questions.question_text: When mimicking the use of a screwdriver a patient rotates his arm at the shoulder but fixes his elbow. Which of the following could be diagnosed with the above presentation?
questions.explanation: Apraxia is defined as the inability to carry out a motor act despite the absence of sensory or motor deficits

questions.question_text: A patient is asked to prepare a sandwich in order to test her ability to perform a sequence of acts. This test is aimed at demonstrating which of the following?
questions.explanation: Ideational apraxia is an inability to correctly sequence a series of goal-directed acts in spite of the ability to execute the instructions when broken down into single acts

questions.question_text: Syndrome of isolated loss of auditory comprehension and repetition, without any abnormality of speech, naming, reading, or writing is suggestive of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Pure word deafness is a syndrome of isolated loss of auditory comprehension and repetition, without any abnormality of speech, naming, reading, or writing

questions.question_text: A well-educated solicitor develops a sudden cerebrovascular deficit which results in loss of ability to read or write, though he is able to speak reasonably well. The dysfunction produced by the ischaemia is called
questions.explanation: Alexia is the acquired inability to read. Alexia with agraphia is seen in angular gyrus lesions and is associated with Gerstmann syndrome

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT a feature of upper motor neurone lesion?
questions.explanation: Muscle atrophy, fasciculations, absent reflexes, and hypotonia are features suggestive of lower motor neurone lesion

questions.question_text: A 65-year-old patient has been drinking nearly 80 units of alcohol a week for the last 13 years. He has numerous physical complications of alcohol use including cirrhosis and cerebellar degeneration. Which of the following is NOT a feature of cerebellar dysfunction?
questions.explanation: Cerebellar limb ataxia is characterized by dysmetria (past pointing), intention tremor, dysdiadochokinesia, and excessive rebound of outstretched arms against a resistance that is suddenly removed

questions.question_text: In a road traffic accident, a 34-year-old man sustains crush injury of the spine. One half of his spinal cord is damaged severely at the level of the tenth thoracic vertebra. Which of the following is a feature of hemisection of the spinal cord?

options.text: The sensory level is at the same level as the lesion (T10)

questions.explanation: Brown–Sequard syndrome is the result of hemisection of the spinal cord

questions.question_text: A patient presents in an agitated state with increased sweating and tremors. On examination she has signs of Grave’s disease. Which is the commonest sign noted in thyroid ophthalmopathy?
questions.explanation: Lid retraction is the most common clinical feature of Grave’s ophthalmopathy

questions.question_text: Headache associated with ipsilateral nasal congestion, rhinorrhea, lacrimation, redness of the eye is characteristic of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Cluster headache is considered as a vascular headache syndrome

questions.question_text: Epilepsy associated with learning disability, shagreen patches, and ash leaf macules are seen in which of the following?
questions.explanation: Tuberous sclerosis is a congenital disease where hyperplasia of ectodermal and mesodermal cells leads to various lesions in the skin, nervous system, heart, kidney and other organs

questions.question_text: Parkinsonian features associated with downward gaze palsy and pseudobulbar dysarthria is characteristic of which of the following conditions?
questions.explanation: Progressive supranuclear palsy is a degenerative neurological disease with parkinsonian symptoms as a prominent clinical feature

questions.question_text: All of the following conditions that affect the trigeminal nerve present with significant sensory loss EXCEPT
questions.explanation: Trigeminal neuralgia is characterized by episodic shooting pain in facial areas supplied by trigeminal nerve

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a cause of bilateral facial nerve palsy?
questions.explanation: Causes of bilateral facial palsy include granulomatous and connective tissue diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus, Sjögren’s syndrome, and sarcoidosis

questions.question_text: A patient known to have bipolar disorder is on lithium. Which of the following will prompt you to check his lithium levels?
questions.explanation: Lithium toxicity results in two major groups of symptoms – neurological and gastrointestinal

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a physical sign noted in anorexia nervosa?
questions.explanation: Lanugo hair is thin, infantile hair noted on the torso and limbs of severely anorexic patients

questions.question_text: Sleep spindles and K complexes on electroencephalogram (EEG) are seen in which of the following phases of sleep?
questions.explanation: During sleep, the body goes through two types of physiological states. This has been divided into REM and NREM phases according to EEG studies

questions.question_text: Electroencephalogram (EEG) is a commonly used diagnostic test. Which of the following statements regarding EEG is NOT correct?

options.text: EEG signals are generated by the cerebral cortex
EEG depends on afferent inputs from subcortical structures, including the thalamus and brainstem reticular formation
Alpha rhythm and sleep spindles are produced by thalamic activity
Diagnostic EEG does not routinely record the activity of the inferior temporal cortex
EEG changes are often very specific to a disease

correct_answer.text: EEG changes are often very specific to a disease

correct_answers.text: EEG changes are often very specific to a disease

questions.explanation: An electroencephalograph represents cerebral cortical activity

questions.question_text: A 32-year-old school teacher is admitted for constipation and acute abdominal pain. She experiences visual and tactile hallucinations with intense anxiety. She develops motor weakness of her legs on administration of hypnotics and diclofenac. Which of the following laboratory tests is indicated?
questions.explanation: This scenario depicts acute intermittent porphyria (AIP)

questions.question_text: Which of the following is NOT helpful in differentiating pseudoseizures from true epileptic seizures?

options.text: Asymmetric movements of limbs and side-to-side movement of the head during ictal activity
Long-lasting seizures that wax and wane over time
Having an established diagnosis of epilepsy in the past

correct_answer.text: Having an established diagnosis of epilepsy in the past

correct_answers.text: Having an established diagnosis of epilepsy in the past

questions.explanation: All of these features except a history of seizure disorder may help to differentiate seizures from pseudoseizures

questions.question_text: Clozapine is strongly associated with fatal agranulocytosis. Which of the following is true regarding clozapine-induced agranulocytosis?

options.text: The risk of agranulocytosis is greatest in the first year
Patients must have weekly blood tests throughout clozapine treatment
After a year blood tests can be discontinued
An amber report from the monitoring body indicates that clozapine should be stopped immediately
A red alert indicates that clozapine could be restarted in a patient who previously had an amber report

correct_answer.text: The risk of agranulocytosis is greatest in the first year

correct_answers.text: The risk of agranulocytosis is greatest in the first year

questions.explanation: Incidence of agranulocytosis in patients on clozapine is less than 1 per 100 patients

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements regarding the dexamethasone suppression test is FALSE?

options.text: Healthy subjects show cortisol suppression on dexamethasone administration
Depressed patients show more cortisol suppression than normal controls
The test has a specificity around 25% to 40% for diagnosing depression
Patients with a positive test may respond better to ECT than those with a negative test
Dexamethasone suppression is not routinely used as a clinical test for depression

correct_answer.text: Depressed patients show more cortisol suppression than normal controls

correct_answers.text: Depressed patients show more cortisol suppression than normal controls

questions.explanation: Exogenous administration of the steroid dexamethasone usually inhibits endogenous cortisol secretion

questions.question_text: Which of the following is an advantage of using CT scan over MRI scan for diagnostic purposes?

options.text: Finer details are seen easily with CT scan
Absence of radiation exposure in CT scan
CT scan is more suitable in pregnant women
CT scan is more immediately available in emergencies
Anterior fossa is better visualized with CT scan

correct_answer.text: CT scan is more immediately available in emergencies

correct_answers.text: CT scan is more immediately available in emergencies

questions.explanation: Immediate availability, especially in head injury units, and ability to enable early detection of hemorrhages make CT scan the preferred diagnostic modality in emergency scenarios

questions.question_text: Choose one of the following conditions where CT scan of the brain is the investigation of choice
questions.explanation: MRI is more sensitive than CT for the detection of lesions of the spinal cord, cranial nerves, and posterior fossa structures

questions.question_text: A patient with bipolar disorder recently stabilized on medications is brought to you with a history of fever for 4 days and blurred vision, muscle fasciculation, hyperactive tendon reflexes, and persistent nausea and vomiting for the last 2 days. Which one of the following may be implicated?
questions.explanation: In this case, a patient’s bipolar disorder has been stabilized on a particular medication

questions.question_text: A patient who has chronic schizophrenia is on a depot antipsychotic medication. Your consultant asks for an ECG. Which of the following will be of most interest to him?
questions.explanation: Prolonged QT interval can predispose to serious ventricular arrhythmia called torsades de pointes

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications has the highest propensity to cause QT prolongation on ECG?
questions.explanation: ECG abnormalities occur in approximately 25% of all patients on antipsychotics

questions.question_text: A patient who is on olanzapine for a long time is developing xanthoma. Which one of the following levels might be elevated in his blood?
questions.explanation: Xanthomas indicate the presence of hyperlipidemia

questions.question_text: Which of the following nutrients, if deficient, can make treatment of depression difficult?
questions.explanation: Though folate deficiency itself is not a common cause of depression, in folate-deficient patients, supplementation might increase response to antidepressant treatment

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a good predictor of metabolic side effects of antipsychotics?
questions.explanation: Waist circumference is a better predictor than baseline weight with respect to metabolic syndrome

questions.question_text: In patients with suspected dementia, which of the following neuroimaging modalities is clinically helpful to differentiate dementia of Lewy body type from Alzheimer’s dementia?
questions.explanation: DAT (dopamine transporter) scan is a SPECT scan that visualizes dopamine transporter

questions.question_text: Which of the following EEG rhythms has the highest frequency?
questions.explanation: Beta >13 Hz, Alpha 8 to 13 Hz, Theta 4 to 7Hz, Delta < 3Hz

questions.question_text: In patients with delirium due to hepatic failure which of the following EEG changes may be seen?
questions.explanation: Slow triphasic waves are typically seen in metabolic encephalopathies such as hepatic failure

questions.question_text: Which of the following suggests successful seizure activity after ECT?
questions.explanation: EEG during ECT treatment shows sharp waves and spikes during the seizure

questions.question_text: In neurological examination, which of the following is seen in hypothyroidism?

options.text: Slow and sluggish deep tendon reflexes
Clonus on testing deep tendon reflexes

correct_answer.text: Slow and sluggish deep tendon reflexes

correct_answers.text: Slow and sluggish deep tendon reflexes

questions.explanation: A characteristic neurological feature associated with hypothyroidism is delayed relaxation of deep tendon reflexes

questions.question_text: Which one of the following patients is not suitable for undergoing MRI investigation when required?

options.text: A 32-year-old woman with last menstrual period 3 months ago
A 74-year-old man with suspected Lewy body dementia
A 53-year-old man with a cardiac pacemaker inserted 10 years ago
A 44-year-old lady with a family history of haemochromatosis
A 22-year-old man with epilepsy and mild learning disability

correct_answer.text: A 53-year-old man with a cardiac pacemaker inserted 10 years ago

correct_answers.text: A 53-year-old man with a cardiac pacemaker inserted 10 years ago

questions.explanation: Insertion of a cardiac pacemaker precludes MRI study as the magnetic field can disturb the pacemaker rhythm

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most clinically useful method of diagnosing Alzheimer’s disease?
questions.explanation: Various guidelines exist for diagnosing dementia. Most of them endorse routinely using clinical interviews for making a diagnosis of dementia
